source_version.content:
Done. The HTML now presents every saying as a unified parallel entry built from your complete supplied Coptic text. fileciteturn2file1L36-L50

Each entry includes:

- **Sahidic Coptic**
- **Approximate Coptic Romanization**
- **Surviving Greek manuscript text**
- **Greek Romanization**
- **Syriac-Aramaic retroversion**
- **Approximate Aramaic pronunciation guide**
- **English translation**

Greek is shown only where an actual Oxyrhynchus witness survives. P.Oxy. 654 contains the Incipit and Sayings 1–7; P.Oxy. 1 preserves portions of Sayings 26–32, incorporates the end of Saying 77 into its Saying 30, and includes an additional saying after 32; P.Oxy. 655 preserves portions associated with Sayings 36–39 and possibly Saying 24. citeturn415140view0turn910792search0turn415140view2turn415140view3

For every other saying, the Greek panel explicitly states **“No surviving Greek manuscript witness”** rather than presenting an invented Greek retroversion. Restored Greek is enclosed in brackets, and physical gaps are represented by ellipses.

The page also has search, jump navigation, language-display toggles, responsive formatting, and print styling.

[Download the complete Coptic–Greek–Aramaic–English HTML edition](sandbox:/mnt/data/Gospel_of_Thomas_114_Coptic_Greek_Aramaic_Parallel.html)
